newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market slipped on Thursday in line with the Italian market, but ended off session lows supported by expectations of benign March consumer price data on Friday, analysts said.
"After recent gains a bit of profit taking was normal," a dealer in Madrid said. "Tomorrow bonos will depend on CPI. If it's good we'll have a rally, but not a significant one".
The market consensus on CPI is for a March yearly rate of 2.4 percent or lower.
"A rate at 2.3 percent will open doors to another rate cut. So it will push the market higher," a dealer said.
"But even so I do not think the market will have the strength to overcome levels at 113.50/60 (long term future)," a dealer said.
Despite the positive outlook for inflation and interest rates, dealers reported selling pressure in the afternoon in the short-end of the yield curve.
Earlier, the Spanish Treasury said it would begin to offer 18-month bills for the first time at the end of April.
"These bills will be better than notes with a similar maturity. So we've started selling notes to make room for these new bills," said a dealer in Madrid.
